preamble: The shift from 'sh' (ʃ) to 'ch' (tʃ) is an affrication process where a post-alveolar fricative gains a stop component, becoming an affricate.

examples.note: English loanwords in various languages often undergo affrication.
Common substitution in early language acquisition.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Muskogean to Eastern Muskogean (Creek, Hitchiti-Mikasuki, Koasati)

examples.note: East of the Mobile–Black Warrior line *š merged with *c/*¢ as the affricate /tʃ/ (Haas 1941). Compare Choctaw shokshi, Chickasaw shokshi'.

examples.to: Hitchiti čolootki, Koasati cholotka, Creek culotkv
examples.note: Compare Choctaw shʋlontʋki. Creek also has variants cvlotkv and Florida Seminole sulotkv.
Compare Choctaw shonkani. The merger is not exceptionless in Alabama, which keeps s in salakla 'goose' (< *šalaklaka) and sokaffi (< *šokaxʷVli).
